text: Fairmont Grain Co-op runs four grain elevators, each wired with moisture, weight, and throughput sensors -- and all of it lands on one aging on-prem SQL Server.
During the six-week harvest window, intake volume spikes eight to ten times the rest-of-year baseline, and that single server chokes right when accuracy matters most.
There's no offsite copy of any of this. If that one room floods or loses power, Fairmont could lose a season's data outright.
And every year, keeping that same fragile hardware alive costs more, without any gain in capacity or reliability.
Next: drawing a hard line around what this migration actually fixes first.
